record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.context_brief: Minimizing nesting depth of indefinite integrals
record.original_question: Design an algorithm that takes an expression built from nested indefinite integrals and returns an equivalent expression whose nesting depth is as small as possible.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 Design an algorithm which finds for a given expression of nested indefinite integrals an equivalent expression for which the the nesting depth is as small as possible.

artifact.status_search_result: The continuous (integral) version of the depth-optimal representation problem appears to remain open. The analogous problem for nested sums has been addressed by Schneider via refined parameterized telescoping algorithms in ΠΣ*-fields (implemented in the Sigma package), which produce sum representations of minimal nesting depth. No analogous complete algorithm for nested indefinite integrals minimizing the integration nesting depth has been reported; recent work on reduction-based and Hermite-style creative telescoping addresses related but distinct optimization goals.

status_evidence.title: Refined telescoping algorithms in RΠΣ-extensions
status_evidence.snippet: (parameterized) telescoping algorithms that can find sum representations with optimal nesting depth in ΠΣ*-fields
status_evidence.claim: Analogous depth-minimization is solved in the discrete (sum) setting, but not the integral setting.
